title: Michigan no-fault: PIP, PPI and residual liability
summary: Follow Rosa through one icy Lansing crash: PIP benefits and the work loss cap, the PIP medical ladder, what PPI pays, and the suits Michigan still allows.
objectives: Tell PIP, PPI and residual liability apart
Name the four PIP benefits and apply the dated work loss cap
Match each PIP medical level to who may choose it
Know when Michigan still allows a suit, including the mini-tort

scenes.title: One crash, three coverages
scenes.src: MCL 500.3101(1),(2), 3105, 3121(1),(5), 3131(1), 3135; DIFS auto FAQ; PSI outline: Automobile Insurance 15% (22 items)

draw.text: Required on every Michigan auto policy

beats.text: Crunch! Rosa slides through a stranger's fence, dents a stranger's properly parked car, and clips Sam's moving car. Sam's fine. Rosa broke her arm.
beats.say: Crunch! Rosa slides through a stranger's fence, dents a stranger's properly parked car, and clips Sam's moving car. Sam's fine. Rosa broke her arm.

beats.text: Every Michigan auto policy must include three coverages.
beats.say: Every Michigan auto policy must include three coverages.

beats.text: Personal injury protection, PIP, pays for injuries, regardless of fault. Property protection insurance, PPI, pays for others' property in Michigan, like fences and properly parked cars.
beats.say: Personal injury protection, P I P, pays for injuries, regardless of fault. Property protection insurance, P P I, pays for others' property in Michigan, like fences and properly parked cars.

beats.text: Residual liability covers your legal liability: injury lawsuits Michigan still allows, and crashes in other states.
beats.say: Residual liability covers your legal liability: injury lawsuits Michigan still allows, and crashes in other states.

beats.say: Rosa gets the hospital bill for her arm. She insures her own car, but the crash was her fault. Who pays?

scenes.title: Michigan Winters Can Snow: four PIP benefits
scenes.src: MCL 500.3107(1)(a)-(c), 3108; memory hook mn_auto-07; matching set ms_personal-08

spots.label: Medical
spots.text: Allowable expenses: reasonable charges for care, recovery and rehabilitation, like Rosa's cast. Up to the PIP medical level chosen.

spots.label: Wages
spots.text: Work loss: income Rosa would have earned in the first 3 years after the accident, cut 15% for the tax advantage, with a cap per 30 days.

spots.label: Chores
spots.text: Replacement services: Rosa can't do laundry or rake leaves with a broken arm, so PIP pays up to $20 a day for help. First 3 years.

spots.label: Survivors
spots.text: Survivor's loss: if an injured person dies, the dependents get the support they lost, for the first 3 years after the accident.

beats.text: Rosa's PIP pays four kinds of benefits. Remember them: Michigan Winters Can Snow.
beats.say: Rosa's P I P pays four kinds of benefits. Remember them: Michigan Winters Can Snow.

beats.text: Tap the four glowing spots.
beats.say: Tap the four glowing spots.

reveal.text: Exam names: Medical is allowable expenses, up to the level chosen. Wages is work loss. Chores is replacement services, up to $20 a day.
reveal.say: Exam names: Medical is allowable expenses, up to the level chosen. Wages is work loss. Chores is replacement services, up to twenty dollars a day.

reveal.text: Survivors: dependents' lost support after a death. All but medical stop 3 years after the accident.
reveal.say: Survivors: dependents' lost support after a death. All but medical stop three years after the accident.

scenes.title: Rosa's paycheck: 85%, then the cap
scenes.src: MCL 500.3107(1)(b); DIFS Bulletin 2026-20-INS; memory hook mn_auto-08
scenes.plain: Lost pay for 3 years after the accident. PIP pays 85% (unless you prove a smaller tax advantage), as the benefit isn't taxed. Capped per 30 days.
scenes.example: Rosa crashed Nov 15, 2026. 85% of her $10,000 a month is $8,500. That date's cap is $7,455, so PIP pays her $7,455 per 30 days.
scenes.exam: Cap: $7,455 per 30 days for accidents Oct 1, 2026 to Sep 30, 2027. It changes every Oct 1: go by the accident date.

beats.text: I can't work for months!
beats.say: I can't work for months!

beats.text: Work loss pays her lost income, minus 15%, because the benefit isn't taxed.
beats.say: Work loss pays her lost income, minus fifteen percent, because the benefit isn't taxed.

beats.text: She earns $10,000 a month, so 85% is $8,500.
beats.say: She earns ten thousand dollars a month, so eighty-five percent is eight thousand five hundred dollars.

beats.text: For accidents from October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027, Michigan's cap is $7,455 per 30 days. Rosa crashed on November 15, 2026, so that's what she gets.
beats.say: For accidents from October first, twenty twenty-six, through September thirtieth, twenty twenty-seven, Michigan's cap is seven thousand four hundred fifty-five dollars per thirty days. Rosa crashed on November fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, so that's what she gets.

beats.text: The cap changes every October 1. Pick it by the accident date.
beats.say: The cap changes every October first. Pick it by the accident date.

scenes.title: Climb the PIP ladder
scenes.src: Policies issued or renewed after July 1, 2020: MCL 500.3107c(1),(3),(4); 3107d(1),(7); 3109a(2),(5); mn_auto-01, 02
scenes.hook: Climb the PIP ladder: 50 - 250 - 500 - the Sky. Or step off the ladder completely (opt-out).
items: $50,000: named insured on Medicaid; household has QHC, Medicaid or other PIP
$250,000: insurer must also offer a QHC (qualified health coverage) exclusion
$500,000, or the Sky: unlimited (default if no valid choice)
Step off (opt out): Medicare A and B; household has QHC or other auto PIP

beats.text: For policies issued or renewed after July 1, 2020, the named insured picks a medical level. Climb the PIP ladder: 50, 250, 500, the Sky.
beats.say: For policies issued or renewed after July first, twenty twenty, the named insured picks a medical level. Climb the P I P ladder: fifty, two hundred fifty, five hundred, the sky.

beats.text: $50,000 is only for a named insured on Medicaid, with the household covered.
beats.say: Fifty thousand dollars is only for a named insured on Medicaid, with the household covered.

beats.text: At $250,000, the insurer must also offer to exclude people with QHC: qualified health coverage, which covers auto injuries with a capped deductible. An excluded named insured needs QHC other than Medicare.
beats.say: At two hundred fifty thousand dollars, the insurer must also offer to exclude people with Q H C: qualified health coverage, which covers auto injuries with a capped deductible. An excluded named insured needs Q H C other than Medicare.

beats.text: No rung at $100,000. No valid choice? You get the Sky, unless the premium paid shows another level.
beats.say: No rung at one hundred thousand dollars. No valid choice? You get the sky, unless the premium paid shows another level.

beats.text: Or step off: opt out of PIP medical, with Medicare Parts A and B, if the household has QHC or other auto PIP. Medicare A and B counts as QHC.
beats.say: Or step off: opt out of P I P medical, with Medicare Parts A and B, if the household has Q H C or other auto P I P. Medicare A and B counts as Q H C.

scenes.title: Dana's call: can Grandma step off?
scenes.src: MCL 500.3107c(1)(a); 3107d(1),(2),(7)(b)-(c); hook mn_auto-02; questions auto-019, auto-020

beats.text: Rosa's grandma renews her policy. She and Grandpa, the only other person at home, both have Medicare Parts A and B.
beats.say: Rosa's grandma renews her policy. She and Grandpa, the only other person at home, both have Medicare Parts A and B.

beats.text: She wants no PIP medical. What does Dana say?
beats.say: She wants no P I P medical. What does Dana say?

options.label: Sorry, everyone must carry PIP medical
options.fail: A named insured with Medicare Parts A and B may opt out of PIP medical, if the spouse and resident relatives have QHC or other auto PIP.

beats.text: Grandma keeps paying for PIP medical she was allowed to drop.
beats.say: Grandma keeps paying for P I P medical she was allowed to drop.

options.label: Pick $50,000: that's the senior level
options.fail: Medic-aid gets a little aid: the $50,000 level is only for a named insured on Medicaid, with the household covered.

beats.text: There's no senior level. $50,000 is only for Medicaid, and Grandma has Medicare.
beats.say: There's no senior level. Fifty thousand dollars is only for Medicaid, and Grandma has Medicare.

options.label: Yes, you can step off the ladder
options.win: Opt-out needs Medicare Parts A and B, a household with QHC or other auto PIP, and proof from the QHC provider. Medicare A and B counts as QHC.

beats.text: Off the ladder I go!
beats.say: Off the ladder I go!

beats.text: Grandpa's Medicare counts as qualified health coverage, so your household passes.
beats.say: Grandpa's Medicare counts as qualified health coverage, so your household passes.

draw.text: Medicare A and B, household covered, QHC proof given

reveal.text: Memory trick: Medic-aid gets a little aid. Medic-are folks are allowed out, if the household is covered.
reveal.say: Memory trick: Medic-aid gets a little aid. Medic-are folks are allowed out, if the household is covered.

scenes.title: The fence and the parked car
scenes.plain: Pays, without regard to fault, for damage your car does in Michigan to other people's property. Up to $1 million per accident.
scenes.example: Rosa's slide wrecked a stranger's fence and dented a stranger's properly parked car. Her PPI pays for both.
scenes.exam: Not moving cars, not your own car, and not outside Michigan. A car parked without unreasonable risk IS covered.

draw.text: In Michigan only, up to $1 million per accident

beats.text: PPI pays, without regard to fault, for damage your car does in Michigan to others' property, up to $1 million per accident.
beats.say: P P I pays, without regard to fault, for damage your car does in Michigan to others' property, up to one million dollars per accident.

beats.text: So Rosa's PPI pays for the fence and the parked car.
beats.say: So Rosa's P P I pays for the fence and the parked car.

beats.text: The rhyme: Moving cars? PPI's not paying. Fences, buildings, properly parked cars in the mitten? PPI's paying, up to a million.
beats.say: The rhyme: Moving cars? P P I's not paying. Fences, buildings, properly parked cars in the mitten? P P I's paying, up to a million.

cards.text: Rosa's slide flattens a neighbor's mailbox in Lansing.
cards.why: Others' tangible property, damaged in Michigan: PPI pays, without regard to fault.

cards.text: Sam's car, moving in the next lane, gets clipped.
cards.why: Vehicles are excluded unless properly parked. Sam looks to collision coverage, or the mini-tort: a small claim against Rosa (coming up).

cards.text: Rosa sideswipes a car parked legally at the curb in Lansing.
cards.why: Parked so as not to cause unreasonable risk: PPI pays.
PPI doesn't pay for your own car. That's for collision coverage. Rosa was over 50% at fault, so limited collision wouldn't pay; broad form would.

cards.text: What if Rosa had slid into a bakery wall in Toledo, Ohio?
cards.why: No PPI outside Michigan. Residual property damage liability, at least $10,000, covers damage in other states.

cards.text: What if her car had smashed the front of Tony's Pizza in Detroit?
cards.why: A building in Michigan: PPI pays.

beats.text: Your turn: does PPI pay?
beats.say: Your turn: does P P I pay?

reveal.text: PPI pays for others' property in Michigan. Not moving cars, not your own car, and nothing outside Michigan.
reveal.say: P P I pays for others' property in Michigan. Not moving cars, not your own car, and nothing outside Michigan.

reveal.text: Out of state, residual property damage liability pays. That's why its minimum of $10,000 still matters.
reveal.say: Out of state, residual property damage liability pays. That's why its minimum of ten thousand dollars still matters.

scenes.title: What you can still sue for in Michigan

draw.text: Michigan: most tort liability is gone. Three of the five that survive:
Also: a nonresident's economic loss, with a threshold injury
Death, serious Impairment, permanent serious Disfigurement
Sue the at-fault driver for the other $150,000
Car damage that insurance didn't pay

beats.text: Now, lawsuits. Tort liability, legal responsibility for harm you cause, is mostly abolished in Michigan for insured vehicles. Five kinds survive: intentional harm, a nonresident's economic loss with a threshold injury, and these three.
beats.say: Now, lawsuits. Tort liability, legal responsibility for harm you cause, is mostly abolished in Michigan for insured vehicles. Five kinds survive: intentional harm, a nonresident's economic loss with a threshold injury, and these three.

beats.text: One: pain and suffering, called noneconomic loss. DID it happen? Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement. Serious impairment has no minimum duration.
beats.say: One: pain and suffering, called noneconomic loss. Did it happen? Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement. Serious impairment has no minimum duration.

beats.text: Had Sam suffered a serious impairment, he could sue Rosa for pain and suffering, and her residual liability would cover it.
beats.say: Had Sam suffered a serious impairment, he could sue Rosa for pain and suffering, and her residual liability would cover it.

beats.text: Two: economic loss above your PIP limits, like medical bills past your level. Sue the at-fault driver for the rest.
beats.say: Two: economic loss above your P I P limits, like medical bills past your level. Sue the at-fault driver for the rest.

beats.text: Three: the mini-tort, up to $3,000 for car damage that insurance didn't pay, in accidents after July 1, 2020. It's not part of required residual liability.
beats.say: Three: the mini-tort, up to three thousand dollars for car damage that insurance didn't pay, in accidents after July first, twenty twenty. It's not part of required residual liability.

beats.text: Watch out: more than 50% at fault? No pain and suffering, and no mini-tort.
beats.say: Watch out: more than fifty percent at fault? No pain and suffering, and no mini-tort.

scenes.title: Sam's call: who fixes his car?
scenes.src: MCL 500.3123(1)(a); 500.3135(3)(e),(4); questions auto-031, auto-035; hook mn_auto-17

beats.text: Back to Sam. His car was moving. He's insured, and Rosa was fully at fault.
beats.say: Back to Sam. His car was moving. He's insured, and Rosa was fully at fault.

beats.text: $2,400 of damage, and no collision coverage. Now what?
beats.say: Two thousand four hundred dollars of damage, and no collision coverage. Now what?

options.label: Claim Rosa's PPI
options.fail: PPI excludes vehicles unless parked without unreasonable risk. A moving car gets no PPI.

beats.text: Rosa's insurer says no: PPI won't pay for a moving car.
beats.say: Rosa's insurer says no: P P I won't pay for a moving car.

options.label: Give up. No-fault means no suing.
options.fail: Michigan abolished most tort liability, but kept the mini-tort: up to $3,000 for car damage that insurance didn't pay.

beats.text: Sam pays the $2,400 himself. He didn't have to: the mini-tort survives.
beats.say: Sam pays the two thousand four hundred dollars himself. He didn't have to: the mini-tort survives.

options.label: Mini-tort: claim the $2,400 from Rosa
options.win: Mini-tort: up to $3,000 from the at-fault driver for car damage that insurance didn't pay. Sam was not more than 50% at fault.

beats.text: Sam takes Rosa to small claims court and recovers his $2,400. It's under $3,000.
beats.say: Sam takes Rosa to small claims court and recovers his two thousand four hundred dollars. It's under three thousand dollars.

reveal.text: A moving car's owner looks to collision coverage, or the mini-tort: the three-grand small-claims fix.
reveal.say: A moving car's owner looks to collision coverage, or the mini-tort: the three grand small claims fix.

scenes.q: In Michigan, suing a negligent insured driver for noneconomic loss (pain and suffering) requires:
choices: Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement
An injury that lasts at least 1 year
Any injury that needed hospital care
scenes.why: That's the tort threshold for noneconomic loss. Serious impairment has no minimum duration, and $3,000 is the mini-tort amount, not a threshold.

beats.text: Quick check. What does a pain-and-suffering suit require?
beats.say: Quick check. What does a pain-and-suffering suit require?

reveal.text: Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement, with no minimum duration.
reveal.say: Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement, with no minimum duration.

items.text: Rosa's hospital bills and lost wages
items.why: PIP pays medical expenses and work loss without regard to fault.

items.text: A homeowner's fence Rosa knocks down in Kalamazoo
items.why: PPI pays for damage to tangible property in Michigan without regard to fault.

items.text: A car Rosa rear-ends in Toledo, Ohio
items.why: PPI is not payable for out-of-state accidents; property damage liability applies anywhere in the US and Canada.

items.text: Someone to do Rosa's housework for a few months
items.why: Replacement services, up to $20 a day, are a PIP benefit.

items.text: A pedestrian with a serious impairment sues Rosa
items.why: Tort liability for noneconomic loss remains when the threshold injury is met.

items.text: Rosa sideswipes a legally parked car in Detroit
items.why: PPI covers a vehicle parked so as not to cause unreasonable risk of the damage.

beats.text: Last one: which coverage pays each loss?
beats.say: Last one: which coverage pays each loss?

reveal.text: Injury benefits: PIP. Others' property in Michigan: PPI.
reveal.say: Injury benefits: P I P. Others' property in Michigan: P P I.

reveal.text: Injury suits and out-of-state damage: residual liability.
reveal.say: Injury suits and out-of-state damage: residual liability.

items: PIP: injuries, regardless of fault. Medical, Wages, Chores, Survivors

PPI: others' property in Michigan, up to $1 million; no moving cars
Suits include: DID threshold, excess economic loss, $3,000 mini-tort
